stemBlocks.value: The graph represents the equations 4x + y = 11 and 2x − y = 1. (a) Write down the graphical solution. (b) Verify the solution by substituting it into both equations. (c) State the x-intercept of each line.
Think first: The lines are already drawn, so the work is careful reading followed by an algebraic check.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p137-q08 from workbook page 137.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the point where the two lines cross.

contentBlocks.value: The lines meet 2 across and 3 up

strategyBlocks.value: Read the crossing point from the graph, substitute those values into both equations to verify, then find where each line meets the x-axis by setting y = 0.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) x = 2, y = 3  (b) 4(2) + 3 = 11 ✓ and 2(2) − 3 = 1 ✓, so the solution is verified  (c) x-intercepts: x = 2.75 for 4x + y = 11 and x = 0.5 for 2x − y = 1.

whyThisWorks.value: A graph can only be read to the accuracy of the grid, so substitution is what proves a read-off is exact rather than close. An intercept is found by setting the other variable to zero, because every point on the x-axis has y = 0 — this works for any equation, whether or not it has been rearranged.

commonErrors.misconception: Verifying in only one equation, which cannot distinguish the true solution from a near miss.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Verifying in only one equation, which cannot distinguish the true solution from a near miss.

commonErrors.misconception: Setting x = 0 when the x-intercept is wanted.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Setting x = 0 when the x-intercept is wanted.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading the intercept of 4x + y = 11 as 11 — that is the y-intercept.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading the intercept of 4x + y = 11 as 11 — that is the y-intercept.

examTip.value: “Verify” means substitute and show both sides balance; a bare restatement of the answer earns nothing.
